source_text: Quomodo ergo quod a necessario venit, possibili meo adscribi non potest; ita quod a possibili venit, necessario adscribi non potest. Id est, quomodo natura corporis et animi mei voluntati meae applicari non potest, ut ideo sic videar esse quia volui, cum non potuerim velle antequam essem, ita malum voluntatis naturae non potest admoveri, ut necessitati possibilitatis opera misceantur.
pass_a_gloss: How therefore what comes from the necessary cannot be ascribed to my possible; so what comes from the possible cannot be ascribed to the necessary. That is, how the nature of my body and mind cannot be applied to my will, so that I may therefore seem to be thus because I willed, when I could not have willed before I was, so an evil of will cannot be applied to nature, so that works of possibility are mixed with necessity.

lemmas.lexica: LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Just as what comes from necessity cannot be attributed to my possibility, so what comes from possibility cannot be attributed to necessity. That is, the nature of my body and mind cannot be assigned to my will, as though I were this way because I willed it, since I could not will before I existed. Likewise, the will’s evil cannot be attached to nature, mixing the works of possibility into necessity.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian contrasts opportunity/help with imposed necessity; load-bearing against natural compulsion to sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
